name: UIBridgeStateMachinePage

states.name: Page Structure and Header
states.description: The page has a persistent header with the title (dynamic: active config name, or 'UI Bridge States' when no config is selected), a config dropdown, and a Refresh button. Below the header the ObservationsPanel appears when a config is active, then an 8-tab navigation bar.
states.precondition: No configuration is selected in the dropdown

states.name: 8-Tab Navigation Bar
states.description: The tab bar contains exactly 8 tabs: Discovery, Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Diagram, Pathfinding, Exploration Results, Export. Tabs are registered with the UI Bridge SDK as 'sm-tab-{value}' elements. The active tab renders its content; inactive tabs are hidden (except Exploration Results, which is off-screen via absolute positioning so the SDK can still scan its severity elements).

states.name: Empty States (No Config Selected)

requiredElements.text: Select a configuration to view the state graph
Select a configuration to view states
Select a configuration to view transitions

states.description: When no configuration is selected, the six config-dependent tabs (Graph Editor, State View, Transitions, Diagram, Pathfinding, Export) each show a tab-specific empty message prompting the user to select a configuration. The Discovery tab always shows its content since it is used to create configs, not depend on them.
states.precondition: Graph Editor tab is active and no configuration is selected

states.name: Observations Panel (Drift Score and Invalidation Log)
states.description: When a configuration is active, an ObservationsPanel appears between the header and tabs. It shows the latest drift fit_score (green ≥0.9, yellow 0.75–0.9, red <0.75), with 'Re-derive all' and 'Invalidate spec observations' action buttons, and an invalidation log table with columns: When, Reason, By, Fingerprints, Action. Rows within 24 h of invalidation have an active Undo button; expired rows show 'expired'.

states.name: Discovery Tab — Phase 1: Connect

requiredElements.text: Click Scan to find apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed.

states.description: The Discovery tab's first phase is a 'Connect to SDK App' card. It contains a 'Scan for Apps' button that discovers running web and desktop apps with the UI Bridge SDK installed. Discovered apps appear as a list, each with a 'Connect' button. After connection, a green success banner shows 'Connected: {appName}'. Phase 1 is hidden once co-occurrence data has been collected.
states.precondition: Discovery tab is active and no co-occurrence data has been collected

states.name: Discovery Tab — Phase 2: Collect (Analyze, Explore, Record)
states.description: Three collection sub-tabs let users provide co-occurrence data before running state discovery. 'Analyze Source' (always enabled) imports a static analysis JSON or generates one for the runner. 'Explore' and 'Record' are enabled only when connected to a live app. Explore runs automated interactions; Record captures a manual session. Both produce co-occurrence data for Phase 3.
states.precondition: Discovery tab is active and no co-occurrence data has been collected

states.name: Discovery Tab — Phase 3 & 4: Discover and Save
states.description: After co-occurrence data is collected, the connect/collect panels hide and discovery controls appear. 'Discover States' runs the fingerprint-based state discovery algorithm (Tauri command ui_bridge_discover_states_from_fingerprints, with JS fallback). Results show a preview of discovered states. 'Save Configuration' (or auto-save via discover-and-save) creates a named config and switches to the Graph Editor tab.
states.precondition: Co-occurrence data has been collected (explore, record, or static import completed)

states.name: Graph Editor Tab
states.description: A ReactFlow-based interactive canvas displaying the state machine as a directed graph. When a config is loaded, states appear as nodes and transitions as edges. An 'Add Transition' FAB overlays the top-left of the canvas. Clicking a state opens the StateDetailPanel side panel on the right; clicking a transition opens the TransitionEditor. Element drag creates transitions (plain drag) or moves elements between states (Alt+drag). A pathfinding highlight overlays a color-coded traversal path on matching edges.
states.precondition: Graph Editor tab is active and a configuration is selected

states.name: State Provenance Badge
states.description: Each selected state in the graph side panel shows a ProvenanceBadge indicating its lifecycle status in the observation-driven pipeline. 'observed' (green) has real captured observations; 'ai-fallback' (yellow) was recently invalidated and is being rebuilt; 'ai-generated' (gray) has no discovery artifact match. Metadata shows observation count and age for observed, or invalidation age for ai-fallback.
states.precondition: A state with provenance='observed' is selected in the graph

states.name: State View Tab
states.description: The State View tab renders StateViewPanel from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine, showing a list of all states with their elements, element thumbnails, and capture screenshots. Selecting a state updates the shared selectedStateId. The empty state message 'Select a configuration to view states' appears when no config is loaded.
states.precondition: State View tab is active and a config with at least one state is selected

states.name: Transitions Tab
states.description: The Transitions tab renders TransitionsPanel showing the list of transitions with source/target states, action types, and runtime introspection data. When the tab opens with an active config, the runner API is queried for permitted and blocked triggers, surfacing the live state machine execution context alongside the static transition list.
states.precondition: Transitions tab is active and a config with transitions is selected

states.name: Diagram Tab

requiredElements.text: Select a configuration to view the diagram

states.description: The Diagram tab renders a Mermaid state diagram for the active config via DiagramTab from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine. It shows a refresh control. When the state count exceeds ~50 (DIAGRAM_MAX_NODES), an 'unavailable' reason is displayed instead of rendering.
states.precondition: Diagram tab is active and a config with ≤50 states is selected

states.name: Pathfinding Tab

requiredElements.text: Select a configuration to use pathfinding
Select a configuration to use pathfinding

states.description: The Pathfinding tab renders PathfindingPanel from @qontinui/workflow-ui/state-machine. Users select start and end states and compute the shortest path. Successful results are passed to the graph via onPathFound, highlighting the traversal path on Graph Editor edges.
states.precondition: Pathfinding tab is active and no configuration is selected

states.name: Exploration Results Tab
states.description: Renders StateExplorationResultsViewer. Uniquely, this tab's container uses absolute off-screen positioning (left: -9999px, 1×1px) when inactive instead of display:none, so the UI Bridge SDK can scan severity elements at any time. The viewer shows exploration run history, state coverage metrics, and discrepancy details grouped by severity (critical, warning, info) via data-testid attributes.
states.precondition: At least one exploration run has been completed

states.name: Export Tab
states.description: ExportPanel with heading 'Export', config summary (name, state count, transition count), and two action buttons: 'Save to File' (Tauri native dialog, writes JSON) and 'Load into Runtime' (POST /state-machine/load). Exported format is UIBridgeRuntime.from_dict() compatible.
states.precondition: Export tab is active and a configuration is selected

description: Visual GUI automation page (UIBridgeStateMachinePage) — a comprehensive state machine builder and explorer backed by the UI Bridge SDK. The page hosts 8 tabs: Discovery (4-phase workflow to build a config from live exploration, recording, or static source analysis), Graph Editor (interactive ReactFlow canvas with side panels), State View, Transitions (with runtime permitted/blocked introspection), Diagram (Mermaid rendering), Pathfinding, Exploration Results (automated verification viewer), and Export. All config-dependent tabs show an empty-state message until a configuration is selected from the header dropdown. When a config is active, an ObservationsPanel above the tabs shows drift-fit scores, re-derivation controls, and the invalidation log for the observation-driven state definition pipeline.
